title: SpinalExpect_NonInvasive
description: This dataset contains non-invasive electrophysiological recordings from the human cervical spinal cord in 30 healthy young adults, collected to test whether temporal expectation influences initial sensory processing in the spinal cord. Participants received electric median nerve stimulation at the left wrist after an auditory cue, with the cue-stimulus interval either fixed at 1100 ms or varied randomly between 100 and 2100 ms. Participants silently counted rare double-stimulus trials (80 ms ISI) and reported the count at the end of each block.
methods_description: Electrodes were placed in three rings (caudal, middle, cranial) around the neck, adapted from Chander et al. (2022). Each trial consisted of an auditory cue followed by median nerve stimulation. Constant-interval and variable-interval blocks alternated, with the starting block type counterbalanced across subjects. Each subject except sub-24 completed two testing days.
